project: Bloor Street West pilot, Shaw Street to Avenue Road
treatment_type: Moving-lane availability reduced in peak periods; curb parking also removed/reconfigured
treatment_detail: One through motor lane each direction at all hours after conversion. Before, curb parking allowed additional moving lanes primarily in peak direction during peak periods; off-peak capacity therefore was not a simple four-to-two conversion. Turn lanes and later signal timing changes were included.
evidence_tier: Downloaded before/after volumes and driving times; descriptive network evidence

sources.title: Bloor Street West Bike Lane Pilot Project Evaluation

data_coverage: June 2016, October 2016, June 2017. Three consecutive weekdays per corridor, 24-hour video at 11 sites; GPS driving runs on three weekdays per corridor in AM/midday/PM.
observed_result: Bloor bicycles 3309 to 4925 (+48.84%); motor vehicles 24322 to 20434 (-15.99%). Sum of Bloor/Dupont/Harbord corridor-average bicycle counts 8896 to 9267 (+4.17%); corresponding motor count index 58315 to 56478 (-3.15%). Bloor peak-direction driving +120 seconds AM and +255 seconds PM.
controls: Dupont/Harbord are plausible spillover roads, not untreated controls. Danforth is used only for the separate economic study.
key_limitations: Each corridor count is an average across separate sites. Sum is a count index, not an audited common screenline, unique people or journeys.
Only three measurement waves; raw daily site records have not been obtained.
Weather, ongoing background changes and signal retiming remain confounders.
49% includes Bay Street; 56% excludes the Bay site outside the pilot. Dry-day-only reported increase is nearly 70%. These are different estimands, not interchangeable.
Attachment gives October Bloor vehicles 19918; main report gives 19919. This reconstruction consistently uses Attachment 1.
improvement_over_nyc: Counts all bicycles and motor vehicles on treatment and diversion roads with contemporaneous driving runs; avoids estimating all cycling from bikeshare share.
next_required_data: Obtain original dated, directional site observations and GPS runs, unexposed comparison roads, vehicle occupancy/classification and subway/bus passenger counts with matched time windows.

date_precision: Opened Monday morning July 13; installation July 10-13
treatment_type: Southbound moving lane converted to protected cycling; northbound sidewalk converted to cycling
treatment_detail: West curb vehicle lane became southbound bicycle lane, east sidewalk became northbound bicycle path, pedestrians consolidated on west sidewalk. Connecting street and turn changes co-occurred.
evidence_tier: Downloaded daily directional bike/pedestrian/vehicle records; official bicycle counterfactual reported but not independently replicated

sources.title: Bike lane statistics for Burrard Bridge 2009-2010
Burrard Bridge Reconfiguration and Structural Rehabilitation
sources.pages: 2; Appendix A pp1-2; Appendix B p1

data_coverage: 579 calendar dates; valid total bicycles 562 days beginning June 16, pedestrians 548 beginning June 30, vehicles 523 beginning June 1. Only 25 bike/11 pedestrian/30 vehicle valid days before opening, including installation dates.
observed_result: Six complete date pairs: July 2,3,4,6,7,9 versus July 16,17,18,20,21,23. Daily mean bicycles 3713.67 to 5527.67 (+48.85%), pedestrians 2362.33 to 2647.83 (+12.09%), vehicles 65127.33 to 65114.33 (-0.02%). Not causal. Immediate four-weekday sensitivity gives bicycles +108.58% and vehicles -5.50%, demonstrating substantial window sensitivity.
published_counterfactual: City report estimated 26% more bicycle trips July 13-September 30 than expected without reconfiguration; public metadata describes an Ontario Bike Route correlation for seasonal/weather adjustment. Ontario series, fitted equation and expected daily values are not in this export, so estimate is not independently reproduced here.
travel_time_result: Official TransLink analysis said little/no bus running-time harm. General Burrard driving times unchanged, but east Pacific approaches about +30 seconds peak; Georgia via Thurlow/Pacific +90 seconds AM and +180 seconds PM. These are reported route components, not complete journeys.
transit_available: Reported bus timing only; no passenger loads in export
controls: Ontario Bike Route was used in the City's bicycle model; Granville Bridge was monitored for diversion. Neither independent raw comparison series nor passenger counts acquired.
key_limitations: Very short usable before period; no seasons of pre-trends.
Primary comparison uses six matched days, no weather control, and excludes holiday/fireworks pairs and all-mode missing observations.
Vehicles are not people; bus loads and changing car occupancy remain unknown.
Other False Creek crossings and transit shifts are not reconstructed.
Sixteen dates/modes have directional sums differing from source totals; original totals retained and discrepancies audited.
Whole 2009-10 series crosses Olympics and transport/network changes; a full-period interrupted-time-series regression would be badly confounded without further work.
improvement_over_nyc: Observed directional daily counts of all bicycles, walkers and motor vehicles at a single bridge boundary, rather than bikeshare proxy; direct moving-lane treatment with exact opening date.
next_required_data: Retrieve Ontario comparison counts and original model, weather, other bridge counts, vehicle classification/occupancy, bus loads and GPS travel times; expand outcome boundary to all False Creek crossings.

project: Dunsmuir Street protected two-way bike lane
treatment_type: Three westbound moving lanes reduced to two
evidence_tier: Official design and monitoring reports; raw multimodal panel not acquired

sources.title: Downtown Separated Bike Lanes Status Report, Summer 2011
Downtown Separated Bicycle Lanes Status Report, Spring 2012

observed_result: Published reports describe growing cycling and little change in general traffic volumes/times; some rerouted trips to northern Hornby blocks take approximately 90 seconds longer. No independent all-person treatment effect computed.
controls: Nearby routes share the growing downtown cycling network and may experience diversion; require independent untreated comparison.
key_limitations: Do not conflate Dunsmuir Street with Dunsmuir Viaduct: the viaduct lane was already closed by construction barriers before the bike-lane conversion.
Network co-interventions and 2010 transport disruptions complicate isolated attribution.
Vehicle counts do not measure passenger totals.
improvement_over_nyc: Verified moving-lane reallocation, continuous all-bike counting and official driving-time monitoring.
next_required_data: Download longer bike counter panel and original dated motor/pedestrian count and GPS records; audit lane transition dates by segment.

date_precision: Network open by June 18; individual components opened earlier
lane_conversion_verified: network-level road-space allocation verified; segment cross-sections require audit
treatment_type: Mixed network intervention; protected corridors plus shared space
evidence_tier: Downloaded official 2016 final report and reproduced selected counts/times

sources.title: Centre City Cycle Track Pilot Final Report
Historical transportation data reports and documents

data_coverage: September 2014 baseline and September 2016 final waves, plus interim/winter monitoring. Automated bike counters; manual volumes and GPS/stopwatch driving each collected on a single day per evaluation period.
observed_result: 5 Street CPR underpass 16h bicycles 630 to 2040 (+223.81%); 12 Avenue west of 2 Street 190 to 870 (+357.89%); 8 Avenue west of 3 Street 920 to 1240 (+34.78%). Driving: 5 Street PM 360 to 370 seconds; 12 Avenue AM 340 to 430, PM 690 to 440; 8 Avenue AM 330 to 315, PM 330 to 330. 12 Avenue PM baseline flagged by City as likely construction delayed.
controls: Annual downtown cordon counts could supply broader all-mode outcomes, but a credible untreated comparison and date/boundary audit are still needed.
key_limitations: Shared Stephen Avenue is not the same treatment as removal of moving lanes and must be separated.
Single-day manual/GPS waves are vulnerable to weather, construction and sampling variation.
Concurrent changes in employment and spending are acknowledged by the report.
Network bike totals may count repeat/cross-corridor trips; do not call them unique riders or additional trips.
improvement_over_nyc: Preplanned evaluation, all-bike counts, explicit travel-time measures, and citywide all-mode cordon data as a possible broader outcome.
next_required_data: Obtain per-segment before/after lane geometry, original daily counts/GPS, all-mode cordon records, occupancy and transit passenger loads; model background employment and transport trends.

treatment_type: One northbound moving lane closed to create bike lane; southbound cycling stayed on sidewalk
evidence_tier: Adverse historical observation; short pilot, not a generalizable causal estimate
observed_result: City reported +870 cyclists/day (+39%), -8800 car occupants/day (-9%) and 7500 fewer people crossing per day; early delays up to 20 minutes diminished during week, bus delays 3-4 minutes. Underlying Appendix C table was not available in retrieved HTML, so these are reported results, not reconstructed totals.
person_flow_measured: City reports total people, but underlying counting/occupancy table not retrieved
controls: No credible concurrent untreated comparison identified; Environment Week timing and rapid adaptation matter.
key_limitations: Only one week, with a different direction/design from the 2009 trial.
Cannot interpret the negative bridge total as a citywide mobility loss without network/OD counts.
Short-run disruption must not be pooled with mature lane operation.
improvement_over_nyc: Shows a directly relevant unfavorable case with reported occupant/person counts, avoiding selection of successful cases only.
next_required_data: Retrieve original appendices, occupancy/count protocol, surrounding crossings and dated travel times.

project: Hornby Street protected two-way bike lane
lane_conversion_verified: mixed; predominantly parking reallocation north of Davie
evidence_tier: Treatment-screening caution; exclude full corridor from clean moving-lane pool

sources.title: Downtown Separated Bike Lane Connection to Burrard Bridge and Seawall

observed_result: Design retains two travel lanes on most blocks by removing parking; southern Pacific-to-Davie segment proposes removal of a travel lane. Whole-corridor results would mix these treatment types.
key_limitations: Do not use whole Hornby corridor as proof about converting a moving lane.
As-built geometry on southern segment needs verification before eligibility.
improvement_over_nyc: Useful network mechanism/route diversion evidence after separating treatment segments.
next_required_data: As-built cross sections and matched segment-specific observations.

project: Burrard Bridge renewal and north intersection redesign
date_precision: Completion year confirmed; exact full reopening date not primary-source verified here
treatment_type: Northbound moving lane to cycling, plus bridge approach widening and turn/intersection changes
evidence_tier: Confirmed treatment package; suitable post-period multimodal panel not acquired

sources.title: Burrard Bridge Upgrades and North Intersection Improvements
Potential Granville Bridge Connector - Public Engagement

observed_result: No reconstructed post-2017 effect. 2015 proposal combines midspan moving-lane reduction with widening roughly 100m of approach to preserve intersection capacity, so evaluation would estimate a package rather than isolated lane removal.
key_limitations: Downloaded 2009-2010 all-mode counts do not cover this intervention.
Long construction period, rehabilitation and intersection widening co-occur.
Do not count 2009 and 2017 as independent cases without modeling shared corridor history.
improvement_over_nyc: Potential longer bike count history and documented geometry; not yet a completed new causal estimate.
next_required_data: Pre-construction and mature post-construction motor/passenger/pedestrian series, other crossings, transit and travel-time records; exact construction phases.
